channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic IPO to Drive Blockbuster Gains for Iconiq, Spark, GIC
item.description: By the time Iconiq made its first investment in Anthropic PBC in 2025, the artificial intelligence developer was valued at $183 billion — more than almost any other tech startup in the world — and well on its way to becoming an AI juggernaut. Yet even Iconiq’s later stage bet is now set to bring in massive returns as Anthropic nears its Wall Street debut.The investment firm, which has pumped more than $6 billion into Anthropic, owns a stake worth approximately $17 billion based on the AI company
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Affirm CEO Levchin Sees Strong Demand Ahead of Sam’s Club Partnership
item.description: Max Levchin, founder and CEO of Affirm Holdings, says the company is seeing no slowdown in demand from consumers or retailers, despite concerns about squeezed household budgets and a challenging consumer-spending outlook. Discussing Affirm’s announced exclusive buy now, pay later deal with Sam’s Club, he says the partnership arrives ahead of the holiday season and reflects retailers’ interest in Affirm as a way for customers to pay. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Remain Bearish on Long-Term Treasuries: DoubleLine's Sherman
item.description: Jeff Sherman, deputy CIO of DoubleLine Capital, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Treasuries rallied Thursday as haven demand returned amid concerns about the artificial-intelligence trade and turmoil in the French market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump and Crypto Firm Sued for Profiting From Foreign Government
item.description: Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial, the cryptocurrency venture he co-founded with his sons, were sued by a shareholder in a rival crypto firm over claims the president illegally profited from his office in violation of the US Constitution.
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris and Olga Kharif

item.title: Blackstone's Schwarzman Discovered the AI Revolution by Accident
item.description: Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman explains how Jack ma helped him discover the AI revolution "by accident" in 2015. He shares his story on the next "Leaders With Francine Lacqua." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dax Shepard Falls Out of Edison Research’s Top 50 Podcasts
item.description: As a new wave of YouTube-centric podcasts gain traction, some old favorites are losing ground
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Navient CDS Widen by Most in Eight Years as Debtholders Left Out
item.description: Costs to protect against a default by Navient Corp. rose on Thursday after the company announced a restructuring that will effectively cut bondholders off from the business’ biggest growth area.
item.dc:creator: Josie Reich

item.title: OpenAI Helped Find Potentially Catastrophic Cyber Flaw
item.description: OpenAI’s model helped identify a potentially catastrophic cybersecurity vulnerability in a programming language that runs millions of websites and applications. Greg Brockman, president of OpenAI, and Matthew Prince, CEO of Cloudflare — which helped protect websites before the flaw was publicly exposed — join Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech” to explain how AI is empowering cyber defenders and attackers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Makes Share Deal to Keep Zuckerberg in California
item.description: Meta says it will issue a new class of shares as part of a plan to keep CEO Mark Zuckerberg in California if a proposed wealth tax is passed and potentially help fund growth. The credit risk hit a record high after Meta laid out plans to boost AI spending. Alison Porter, portfolio manager for Janus Henderson's Global Technology Leaders Team, explains how the equities market are weighing these factors. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Doubles Down on AI Spending, Plans New Class C Shares
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Meta's plans to boost AI spending and release new Class C shares to ensure CEO Mark Zuckerberg stays in California if a wealth tax is passed. Plus, Tesla reported strong profit, but a big cut to its spending plans is raising questions about Elon Musk's AI, robotaxi and robotics goals for the company as it weighs a potential merger with SpaceX. And OpenAI's models helped find a potentially catastrophic software vulnerability. OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince explain how AI is enabling both defenders and hackers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla Shareholders Likely to Demand a Premium: New Street's Harwood
item.description: Tesla investors are likely to demand a premium in a possible merger with SpaceX, says Ben Harwood, New Street Research senior analyst for technology and space infrastructure. Harwood discusses the synergies he sees between Tesla and SpaceX and why demand for Tesla's full self-driving shows the company has momentum to keep profits growing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The AI Spending Profit Test, Blackstone's Gray sees "Parabolic" Demand
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Meta tops Wall Street targets, but its AI spending surge raises fresh concerns. Tesla pulls back on spending, while Blackstone President Jonathan Gray pushes back on AI bubble fears. Plus, JPMorgan’s Gabriela Santos and Goldman Sachs’ Ben Snider break down whether the AI boom can deliver profits and where investors find the next winners. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Cuts Deal to Keep Zuckerberg in California Amid Tax Threat
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. shares fell after Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg told investors the company would bet even more aggressively on artificial intelligence. Meta Platforms Inc. is giving Mark Zuckerberg non-voting shares that he can sell to cover a tax bill without relinquishing control of Meta. Bloomberg's Mandeep Singh joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX is 'Most Egregiously Overpriced Company at Scale,' Says George Noble
item.description: Stocks dropped as a jump in oil prices and renewed concerns about the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade pushed global investors toward the safety of bonds. George Noble, Managing Partner at Noble Capital Advisors, discusses the outlook for the AI trade and companies like Coreweave and SpaceX. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: iPhone Duo Review + Pre-Order Problems with Andru Edwards
item.description:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is finally here, but is it worth more than $2,000? In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is joined by Gear Live’s Andru Edwards, who has spent the past week testing the iPhone Duo. They break down its design, software, cameras, battery life and biggest shortcomings, while revealing new details about what Apple is planning for future models. They also debate Apple’s troubled pre-order rollout, which has left many customers waiting months for their devices.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX Works With Apollo, Nvidia on New Grok Partnership Program
item.description: SpaceX is working with Apollo Global Management, Nvidia Corp. and dozens of other firms on a new partnership program to deploy and improve its Grok AI systems, part of a bid to bolster business adoption of its artificial intelligence offerings.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo

item.title: Meta Cuts Tax Deal to Keep Zuckerberg in California
item.description: Meta quietly created a new class of non-voting shares that could give Mark Zuckerberg billions in liquidity without weakening his control of the company. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow explains the regulatory filings, Zuckerberg’s concerns over California’s proposed billionaire tax, and why Meta says the move is also about funding its massive AI ambitions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Credit Risk Gauge Surges to Record on AI Spending Plans
item.description: A measure of Meta Platforms Inc.’s credit risk hit a record high Thursday and its bonds weakened, as plans to ramp up capital spending reignited fears that tech giants will issue more debt for the artificial intelligence buildout in an already saturated market.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua and Katherine Schwartz

item.title: Firms Race to Fix Widespread Cyber Flaw Before Hackers Break In
item.description: Governments and companies around the world rushed Thursday to patch two critical flaws in widely used technology, keeping some websites offline as a precaution against hackers trying to use the flaws for cybercrime.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Big Win Over Meta, New Epstein Case Cast State AG Into Spotlight
item.description: With one landmark courtroom victory this week against Meta Platforms Inc., New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez is poised to bring in almost double the state’s annual revenue.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson, Madlin Mekelburg and Georgia Fearn
